addon.name: Mood Engine
addon.description: Rows built from your own Letterboxd taste, by mood, plus your curated lists and your friends. Never shows what you've already seen (except Old friends and the full Lists).

tonight._doc: Tonight (lib/rows.js, lib/tonight-memory.js). Marco, 14/11/2026 (questionnaire, 'Bigger pool + 30 days without repeating'): each pick is drawn from the top `depth` films of its mood (40; it was 12 since 19/10/2026) and a film that was in Tonight on one of the `noRepeatDays` days before today (30; cache/tonight-memory.json, written by the scheduled night alone) is not drawn, pinned or not. When none of a mood's top `depth` is free the best free film below them is taken, and when the whole mood was shown in that time, the film shown longest ago. depth is a whole number from 1, noRepeatDays a whole number from 0 (0 = no memory); a config without them gets 40 and 30. Marco, 19/10/2026 (questionnaire): the draw is EVEN among those films. bias is the exponent of the first pass's draw, top[floor(rand() ** bias * top.length)]: 1 is uniform, above 1 leans to the very top (it was 1.6 until 19/10/2026), below 1 leans to the last. A positive number. Anything else in any of the three stops the build.

tmdb._doc: Marco, 20/10/2026: a film cached without the `trailer` key was never asked about its trailer; the build asks TMDB again for at most this many of them per run (lib/tmdb.js movie()), and the rest wait for the next night. 0 turns the backfill off. A film cached with `trailer: null` was asked and has none: it is asked again only at its 45-day expiry. The one-off bulk run is scripts/backfill-trailers.js.

exclude._doc: Films that are never recommended (lib/exclude.js, Marco 13/10/2026): out of every Board row, of the moods (rows, picker, the index's mood membership) and of the Discover catalogs of moods and directors. Search, Explore, Lists, Lists unseen and Friends keep them (eligible is untouched). IMDb ids, tt + digits; any other value stops the build. A film listed here must not be in a mood's `pins` (Marco, 15/11/2026: 'Keep the pins, except Paterson'): the build stops and names the film and the moods.

shortRow._doc: maxMinutes: the longest film of ⏱️ Under 95 minutes. minMinutes: THE floor of a feature film, the one number (Marco, 14/11/2026, "Keep shorts only in the Short row"): a film whose known runtime is under it is in no row that recommends a film he has not seen (the mood rows and Tonight, the v2 Board's moods, filters and combined rows, the special rows that recommend, Friends loved, Friends watched this week and this month, Best of your lists, New releases, Under 95 minutes, every Discover cut); the rows that show a source keep their shorts (watchlist, Worth watching again, Friends want to see this too, prizes, list rows, Loved by your directors, Lists, friends' collections). A film with no known runtime is not a short. 0 lets shorts in everywhere (lib/pool.js isShort, minFeatureMinutes).

music._doc: Marco, 22/10/2026. ~03:50 UTC ("in new releases dont recommend that many concert documentaries, im not into kpop, taylor swift" / "i like things that are like are in my letterboxd like stop making sense"): in New releases for you a MUSIC film enters only with evidence from his Letterboxd. ~06:40 UTC (lote 2): the same rule for ALL the rows that recommend (the Board, the cuts by decade, runtime, country and rating, and the catalogs by country and decade still to come), not only New releases. A music film (lib/pool.js isMusicFilm: TMDB genre Music and, Documentary or a live keyword (15, among them concert, live concert, touring, musical performance) or Tour/Live/Concert/Unplugged/In Cinemas as a whole word in the title; it also marks a fiction film that has the Music genre and a live keyword, such as Trap, A Star Is Born) that he has not seen is recommended only with: a director he rated in 2+ films or an artist in 3+ with weight above 0.12 (the card's own thresholds, lib/taste.js personEvidence), OR the film is on his watchlist, OR it is in a list of trust critic or director. The rows that SHOW what a source holds do not ask it (your watchlist, Friends want to see this too, the prize row, the single-list rows, Loved by your directors, Lists, Lists (unseen), Friends, Search); Friends watched this week and month DO ask it. The Worker reads the verdict from the index (bit 8 of the flags) in Moods, Explore and the profiles' Tonight, Under 100 min and themes. README.md "The music rule" has the table. Risk he accepted: a show of a new artist disappears from the Board until he rates something of the person or puts it on the watchlist. The session's choice, not Marco's: the key is Marco's config only; lib/people.js deriveConfig does not copy it, so the profiles built per person (Will) keep their rows as they were. The first version of the key was newReleases.musicNeedsEvidence (still read when this one is absent: lib/pool.js musicOptions). Set needsEvidence to false to put every row back. Marco, 22/10/2026 ~15:15 UTC (questionnaire "Music 1 of 4"): the mood Music is EXEMPT from this rule in its own option of the Moods menu ("it is the only place where I ask for music when I open the app"): exemptMoods lists the mood ids; the static addon's Discover Moods option and the Worker's Moods option (index rules.musicExemptMoods) show the music films with no evidence, and no other surface does (the Board rows, Tonight, the cuts by country, decade and genre, Explore, the profiles, Friends watched, New releases; Search finds a held-back film by its name alone). The profile /p/marco mirrors the main address, so its Moods option Music is exempt too. Risk he accepted: K-pop and Taylor Swift shows appear inside Music, in the order of his taste. An empty list or no key puts the rule back in that option.

insideKeywords.noir: Marco, 15/11/2026 (questionnaire, Noir): "Everything with "noir" in the tag, as before". The only positive term that matches inside any TMDB keyword (film noir, neo-noir, tech noir, future noir, horror noir …); the family scores once. Every other positive term matches the whole keyword or a compound its recipe names (lib/moods.js).

all._doc: Marco, 28/10/2026 (Discover proposal 5): the option 'All friends loved' of the Friends menu of the Worker's index (build.js, lib/friends-option.js): every film in the index that ANYONE of the crowd (the people you follow plus the configured friends) rated at the bar or more and that you have not seen, in the order of the index and spread over the directors. The bar is friendRows.love.minStars unless `minStars` is written here. Ratings ignored (ratingsIgnored) love nothing. Without `word` the option is not made. It is a direct collection, like the other friends options: no recommendation rule. Sits after the Top options and before Watch together.

directorsLoved._doc: Loved by your directors (lib/directors-loved.js, Marco 11/10/2026). Favourites: your ratings (minFilms rated, average minAvg) + include + followed accounts mapped below; exclude always wins. defaultWeight: the taste weight given to an included or followed director with less of their own (about a director you rate 4.3 over 5 films).
